why: All three checks pass, so the gap survives. (1) VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/admin-setup.md line 45 carries the sentence exactly as quoted. Reading the WHOLE line does not reverse it — the remaining two sentences only add the cross-source lock-key carve-out and note that a configured policyHelper makes its output the only source those checks read; line 54 adds that policyHelper 'preempts all four sources'. The table at lines 47-52 names the four: Server-managed (Highest), plist/registry (High, macOS com.anthropic.claudecode / Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode), File-based managed (Medium), Windows user registry HKCU (Lowest). (2) CITED LINES: managed-composition.ts:4 does read 'We have exactly two, and they are the two the documentation names'; :130 is `export type ManagedPolicyWinnerV1 = 'delivered' | 'file' | 'none'`; managed-policy-loader.ts:48 is the darwin file path '/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json'. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier: resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:127-138) has exactly two seams — `file` (loadManagedPiPolicyWithDiagnostics) and `delivered` (getDeliveredManagedPolicy) — and feeds only those into composeManagedPolicySources. Nothing upstream supplies a third. `grep -a` for HKLM/HKCU/HKEY_LOCAL/SOFTWARE\Policies/plist/CFPreferences/systemPreferences/getUserDefault/'reg query' across packages/*/src, apps/electron/src and apps/cli returns only (a) prose comments in managed-composition.ts:29,:44 and config-doctor.ts:12, (b) docs/, (c) an unrelated MachineGuid `reg query` in credentials/backends/secure-storage.ts:105, and (d) vendored bundles under packages/pi-agent-server/dist. No plist reader, no registry reader. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels filter placement, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — none touches a managed delivery channel. NOT a rebrand artefact either: the file channel was ported under Nessy paths (/Library/Application Support/Nessy, /etc/nessy, %ProgramData%\Nessy), so a Nessy-domain plist and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Nessy would be the analogue and neither exists; the fork's dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows are unrelated to MDM policy delivery. It is already recorded as a known open gap at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:694 ('File-channel shape we do not have: drop-in managed-settings.d/ … plus macOS com.anthropic.claudecode managed preferences and Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode … and a lower-priority HKCU tier') — recorded, but as a gap, not as a decision, and the drop-in half of that same list has since been implemented (managed-policy-loader.ts:62 managedPiPolicyDropInDirForPlatform), which leaves the plist/registry half genuinely outstanding. Two framing corrections that do NOT rescue the finding but must not be repeated downstream: the composition module does not hold an unexamined 'two-source assumption' — :27-29 recites the full documented tier (policyHelper > remote > MDM > file-based > HKCU) and :44 says in so many words 'excludes the user-writable HKCU tier, which we do not have'; and the '/status can never say (plist)/(HKLM)/(HKCU)' clause is vacuous restatement, since a label for a channel nothing reads carries no information (config-doctor.ts:16-18 deliberately quotes only the (remote)/(file) half of settings.md:706).
correctedState: Two of the four documented sources exist, not 'only two sources' as an arbitrary shortfall, and the arbitration RULE the quoted sentence states is implemented faithfully for the two we have. Present: the server-managed source (the gateway-delivered payload, packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts) at highest priority, and the file-based managed source (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:44-67, rebranded to /Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json, /etc/nessy/managed-policy.json, %ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json, plus the managed-policy.d/ drop-in directory). composeManagedPolicySources implements priority-order-first-non-empty-wins exactly (managed-composition.ts:191-198: delivered wins wholesale iff carriesManagedSettings(delivered)), including the cross-source lock-key carve-out from the same doc line. Absent: the High-priority OS policy channel (macOS managed-preferences plist, Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies) and the Lowest-priority Windows HKCU tier — the docs themselves call HKCU 'a convenience default rather than an enforcement channel', so the material gap is the tamper-resistant plist/HKLM tier, which for a bank fork sits ABOVE the file channel we do have. policyHelper, the fifth preempting source on the same page (line 54), is also absent; it is out of scope for the server channel by a recorded reason (2026-07-29-delivered-policy-enforcement.md:245-246, server-managed-settings.md:129 says the server channel does not honour it) but not for the file/MDM channels, which is where the docs say it is read from. Channel labels follow the sources rather than the other way round: ManagedPolicyWinnerV1 = 'delivered' | 'file' | 'none' is a faithful two-source label set, and widening it is a consequence of adding readers, not an independent defect.
